<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par111" />''put them'', &c.); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=39|verse=1}}. Finally there are the cases in which an infinitival or participial construction representing past time, according to {{GHGpar|113|r}}, {{GHGpar|116|x}}, is taken up and continued by an imperfect consecutive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|111|r}}
(2) To represent ''present'' actions, &c., in connexion with tenses, or their equivalents, which describe actions and states as being either present or lasting on into the present (continuing in their effect); so especially,

(α) In connexion with the present perfects, described in {{GHGpar|106|g}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=9}} ''therefore my heart is glad'' ({{GHGheb|text=שָׂמַח}}) ''and my glory rejoiceth'' ({{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫גֶל}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=16}} (parallel with a simple imperfect). Cf. also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=29|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫שֶׁב}} (prop. he sat down, ''and has been enthroned'' ever since), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=41|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|111|s}}
(β) In connexion with those perfects which represent experiences frequently confirmed (see {{GHGpar|106|k}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=2}} ''he cometh up'' ({{GHGheb|text=יָצָא}}) ''like a flower, and is cut down'' ({{GHGheb|text=וַיִּמָּל}}); ''he fleeth'' ({{GHGheb|text=וַיִּבְרַח}}) ''also as a shadow'', {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא יַֽעֲמוֹד|translate=and continueth not}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, 11, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=2}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|111|t}}
(γ) In connexion with imperfects which, in one of the ways described in § 107. 2, are used in the sense of the present; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=10}} ''but man dieth'' ({{GHGheb|text=יָמוּת}}) ''and becometh powerless'' ({{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּחֱֽלָשׁ}}), &c., i.e. remains powerless; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=9}}f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (''when thou mockest''), 12:25, 34:24, 37:8 (parallel with a simple imperfect); 39:15. In the apodosis of a conditional sentence, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=16}}, so also after an interrogative imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=42|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=וַתֶּֽהֱמִי}} for which in verse 12 and in 43:5 we have {{GHGheb|text=וּמַה־תֶּֽהֱמִי|translate=and why art thou disquieted?}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|111|u}}
(δ) In dependence on participles, which represent what at present continues or is being repeated, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=2}} ''behold the king weepeth'' ({{GHGheb|text=בֹּכֶה}}) ''and mourneth'' ({{GHGheb|text=וַיִּתְאַבֵּל}}) ''for Absalom''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=5|hidebook=1}}f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=34|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=22 ff.}}, but cf. e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=קֹרֵא לֶֽאֱלוֹהַּ|translate=who called upon God}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽעֲנֵ֫הוּ|translate=and he answered him}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|111|v}}
(ε) In dependence on other equivalents of the present, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=144|verse=3}} (see above, m); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=22}}. So especially as the continuation of an infinitive, which is governed by a preposition (cf. {{GHGpar|144|r}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=92|verse=8}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|111|w}}
(3) To represent ''future'' actions, &c., in dependence on—(α) an imperfect which refers to the future, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=22|hidebook=1}}f.;—(β) a perfect consecutive, or those perfects which, according to {{GHGpar|106|n}}, are intended to represent future events as undoubtedly certain, and therefore as though already accomplished (''perf. propheticum''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=15}} (parallel with a simple imperfect separated from {{GHGheb|text=ו}}); 5:16 (cf. 2:11, 17, where the same threat is expressed by the perfect consecutive); 5:25, 9:5, 10f.,<section end="par111" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
